svg.title: Galadriel offline PID estimand and provenance graph
svg.desc: The graph begins with a versioned PID question that fixes ordered sources, a predeclared target with explicit provenance, the input law, finite-sample acceptance, transforms, row relation, support or gauge, units, paper functional, sample-estimator route, implementation method, implementation entry point, atom coordinates, reference roles, and the exact pid-rs dependency pin. It then separates two implemented offline routes. The categorical route keeps five objects distinct. Its paper functional is functional.shared-exclusions.mgw-categorical. Its raw-row empirical-PMF sample-estimator route is route.shared-exclusions.mgw-empirical-pmf. Its upstream implementation-method catalog identity is shared-exclusions.categorical. Its exact implementation entry points are pid_core::stable::categorical::discrete_sxpid2_with_budget and pid_core::stable::categorical::discrete_sxpid3_with_budget. Raw rows produce a plug-in empirical-PMF estimate. They do not evaluate a separately declared population law. Exact CREBAIN fixture balance makes the empirical PMF coincide with the canonical law for that fixture only. The route uses an explicit resource budget, the Williams-Beer antichain lattice, and the Gutknecht-Wibral-Makkeh part-whole interpretation. Each signed atom equals its informative part minus its misinformative part. Holding the complete source rows fixed while permuting only the target preserves every informative atom but may change misinformative and net atoms. Retained categorical sample-estimator reports use nats, while named aggregate atoms convert once to bits. The continuous route evaluates the related but distinct Ehrlich-Schick-Poland-Makkeh-Lanfermann-Wollstadt-Wibral functional and estimator, with KSG mutual-information constituents and an explicit resource budget, on a declared full-dimensional continuous law and fixed source gauge. All outputs remain nats. Its two-source atoms are redundancy R sub sx, unique one equals I of source one and target minus redundancy, unique two equals I of source two and target minus redundancy, and synergy equals joint-source mutual information minus both marginal mutual informations plus redundancy. The Schick-Poland general construction and the Williams-Beer I-min functional are reference boundaries, not evaluated fallbacks. A bottom firewall distinguishes both PID routes from Galadriel's project-defined Q, which is joint-source mutual information minus the larger marginal mutual information and is not a PID synergy atom. It also separates PID from the target-free pairwise mutual-information graph, BROJA, and other unevaluated measures.
svg.text: Offline PID estimands: two related constructions, never one generic “Wibral PID”
Functional, sample-estimator route, implementation method, entry point, law, gauge, units, and pin define a result.
PidQuestionSpec v3 seals one scientific question before evaluation
E_PID := (ordered S₁,S₂, predeclared T, generated law, acceptance rule, transform, row relation,
support/gauge, native units, aggregate units, paper functional, sample-estimator route, implementation method,
implementation entry point, coordinates, components, aggregation, references, and exact pid-rs pin)
Trial arms are typed separately: coupled-law evaluation versus within-trial target permutation. Functional identity alone is not a scalar identity.
A · CATEGORICAL MAKKEH–GUTKNECHT–WIBRAL SHARED EXCLUSIONS
Five distinct categorical method objects
functional: functional.shared-exclusions.mgw-categorical
sample route: route.shared-exclusions.mgw-empirical-pmf
method/catalog: shared-exclusions.categorical
entry: pid_core::stable::categorical::discrete_sxpid2_with_budget
entry: pid_core::stable::categorical::discrete_sxpid3_with_budget
Raw rows estimate a PMF. Exact-law coincidence is fixture-only.
Role-typed provenance edges
Functional — Makkeh, Gutknecht & Wibral (2021)
Antichain lattice — Williams & Beer (2010). I_min not evaluated.
Part-whole derivation — Gutknecht, Wibral & Makkeh (2021)
Schick-Poland general construction — related, not evaluated
Typed atoms and fixed-source hostile control
A_net(a) = A_info(a) − A_misinfo(a), a ∈ {Red,U₁,U₂,Syn}
source rows fixed, T permuted
⇒ A_info,coupled(a) = A_info,control(a), for every atom a
Misinformative and net parts may change. Signed atoms are never clamped.
Trial reports: nats. Aggregate atoms: bits after one division by ln(2).
B · CONTINUOUS EHRLICH SHARED-EXCLUSIONS PID2
Distinct paper-defined functional and estimator
route = experimental::continuous::pid2_isx_report_with_budget
Declared full-dimensional law · fixed source gauge · no added noise · nats
Role-typed provenance edges
Functional + estimator — Ehrlich et al. (2024), PRE 110, 014115
MI estimator basis — Kraskov, Stögbauer & Grassberger (2004)
Original antichain lattice — Williams & Beer (2010). I_min not evaluated.
Schick-Poland et al. general construction — related, not evaluated here
PID2 atom construction and control interpretation
Red = R_sx · U₁ = I(S₁;T) − Red · U₂ = I(S₂;T) − Red
Syn = I(S₁,S₂;T) − I(S₁;T) − I(S₂;T) + Red
Coupled arm: population-functional estimate under the declared law.
Permutation arm: exchangeable descriptive score, not an i.i.d. independent-law estimate.
Claim firewall — nearby quantities are not interchangeable
Q := I(S₁,S₂;T) − max{I(S₁;T), I(S₂;T)}
Q is project-defined. Q is not a PID synergy atom.
The target-free KSG-MI graph is not PID or fusion evidence.
Categorical and continuous routes are distinct. Atoms are estimand-relative.
BROJA, I_min, and Schick-Poland are not fallback routes.
The diagram states provenance and estimand identity. It does not claim field calibration, causal interpretation, or scientific novelty.
